params.body:
## What

- **Frames get an SEO field**: title, description and share image per language. The site reads it (hoet-eyewear, same branch name). An empty field means the site derives the title ("Couture F2 - Hoet") and the description from the material, as now.
- **Pages use the shared `seo` type** instead of their inline copy. The shape is the same, and some pages already stored `_type: "seo"`, so no data changes.
- **The SEO title says what it is**: the title in Google and on the browser tab, separate from the text on the page. On hoet.be the site adds " - Hoet" at the end, and "Hoet - " in front on the home page.
- **A warning, not an error,** on hoet.be when:
  - the brand is typed in a title (except on the home page), because the site adds it;
  - the title with " - Hoet" passes 60 characters.

  Elsewhere (Cabrio, Hoet Design) only the 60-character warning stays, as before.

## How

The rules live in `schemaTypes/lib/titleRules.ts`. The brand check reuses `onHoetBe` and `isHomePage` from `slugRules.ts`: a frame's brand comes from its collection.

## Checked

- 95 tests pass (`vitest`, without the token-bound `config.test.ts`), including the new `tests/title-rules.test.ts`.
- `tsc`, `sanity schema validate` (0 errors, 0 warnings), `sanity build` and lint pass.
- Not clicked through in a running Studio: that needs a Sanity login.

## After merge

`npm run deploy` for the Studio.
params.title: Give frames an SEO field and warn when a title names the brand
